To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the hairpin diagram is an important mechanism for two-body nonletponic decays; 2) there is no CP asymmetry in pure B u →ππ, B d →ππ decays, but the asymmetry in B u →Kπ decays may be sizable, and the asymmetry in some other channels may be as large as 20%; 3) the branching ratios for some pure modes are on the order of ~10-7, and
(i) the hairpin diagram is a new source of CP violation in B decays and (ii) it is a new source for B decays with a large branching ratio.
the hairpin diagram can significantly enhance the decay rates of the above-mentioned channels and that the CP asymmetries of B u ± →ψ K ± and B d 3 →ψ K s can be large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two-body nonletponic B decay modes, which can occur through the QCD loop-induced diagram.
the effect of the new diagram on B meson nonleptonic decay.
the study of two-body non-leptonic decays of B mesons, which are of great interest in the context of CP violation in B decays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hairpin diagram does exist and it is not negligible.
the hairpin diagram is a new and important source of CP violation in the standard model, which can not be neglected.
the inclusion of the hairpin graph in two-body B decays is necessary to obtain a satisfactory description of the experimental data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hairpin diagram can contribute to the CP violation in B meson systems.
the hairpin diagram plays a crucial role in the nonleptonic two-body B decays.

the hairpin contribution to the decay rates of B u ± →Kπ ± and B d 2 →π K s can be comparable to the penguin one, while the hairpin contributions to the CP asymmetries in these two modes are negligible, and those to the CP asymmetry in B d 0 ( B d 0 )→ψ K s can be as large as 10% (30%).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hairpin diagram is not a small correction to the penguin one.
a number of nonleptonic two-body B decays are expected to be enhanced by a factor of about 3–5, which may be observed in the near future.
the hairpin diagram can be important and must be taken into account when calculating decay rates and CP violation in nonleptonic two-body B decays.
